rows.grounds: name of the bīja syllable hrīṃ; mantra element kept transliterated
locative indicating the body part to be guarded
first member of compound describing the goddess's form
second member of compound qualifying Maheśvarī as seed-formed
epithet of the goddess invoked as protector

items.question: What seed-form manifestation of Maheśvarī protects the forehead within this divine armor?
premises: The verse invokes a protective power for the forehead.
The hrīṃ-syllable is named as the protecting agent.
Maheśvarī is present in a seed-form identified with that syllable.
items.inference: Therefore Maheśvarī, manifest as the hrīṃ-syllable in seed-form, guards the forehead.
items.plain_english: May the hrīṃ-syllable, Maheśvarī in seed-form, protect the forehead.
